components.note: 王 (a variant form of 玉, meaning jade) — 理 originally referred to the natural grain or pattern in jade, later extending to 'reason, logic, to manage.'
里 (lǐ) gives the sound — 理 is also pronounced lǐ, an exact match.
心 (heart/mind) — 想 relates to thinking, missing someone, or wanting something in one's heart.
相 (xiāng) gives the sound — 想 is pronounced xiǎng, matching aside from tone.

example.hanzi: 成为宇航员是他从小的理想。
example.pinyin: Chéngwéi yǔhángyuán shì tā cóngxiǎo de lǐxiǎng.
example.english: Becoming an astronaut was his ideal since childhood.
example.fact: Yuri Gagarin became the first human to reach space in April 1961, orbiting Earth once in the Vostok 1 capsule in about 108 minutes. He experienced weightlessness for nearly the entire flight, an experience so novel that engineers weren't sure a human could function afterward. His safe return proved otherwise and kicked off the space race in earnest.

components.note: 辶 (to walk/move) — shows 过's core meaning of 'passing through' or 'crossing'
咼 (guō) gives a sound close to 过's reading guò; the simplified form 过 now uses 寸 in place of 咼, but the phonetic connection traces back to the traditional character 過
攵 (to act, strike) — 敏 describes being quick and effective in action, 'nimble, sharp.'
每 (měi) is only distantly related in sound to mǐn — the rhyme has drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 我对花生过敏，吃了会全身起疹子。
example.pinyin: Wǒ duì huāshēng guòmǐn, chī le huì quánshēn qǐ zhěnzi.
example.english: I'm allergic to peanuts; eating them makes my whole body break out in hives.
example.fact: A peanut allergy occurs when the immune system mistakenly identifies harmless peanut proteins as a threat and releases histamine in response. Anaphylaxis, the most severe reaction, can constrict airways within minutes, which is why epinephrine auto-injectors work by rapidly relaxing smooth muscle and tightening blood vessels. Peanut allergies affect roughly 1-2% of children in the United States, and unlike some other food allergies, most children do not outgrow it.

components.note: 山 (mountain) sits atop 几 in the modern simplified form; it stands in for the more complex traditional element 豈, an ancient drum-shaped ritual vessel sounded during victory celebrations, the source of 凯's meaning "triumphant, victorious."
几 (jǐ) marks the simplified phonetic element, standing in for the more complex traditional form 豈 (qǐ) — the two readings share a distant historical root even though they no longer sound alike.
牛 (ox) — 特 originally referred to a male ox singled out for sacrifice, a special animal set apart from the herd.
寺 (sì) gives a hint of the sound — 特 is pronounced tè, a connection that has drifted over time.

example.hanzi: 凯特是我们班唯一的美国交换生。
example.pinyin: Kǎitè shì wǒmen bān wéiyī de Měiguó jiāohuànshēng.
example.english: Kate is the only American exchange student in our class.
example.fact: The name Kate is a short form of Catherine, which traces back to the Greek 'Aikaterine,' possibly linked to the goddess Hecate or to the Greek word 'katharos,' meaning pure. Catherine of Alexandria, a 4th-century martyr associated with a spiked wheel, gave rise to the term 'Catherine wheel' for both a torture device and, later, a spinning firework.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — 点 originally related to a small flame or dot of light, giving rise to the meaning 'dot' or 'point.'
占 (zhàn) gives a hint of the sound — 点 is pronounced diǎn, a connection that has drifted over the centuries.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 雨水打在窗户上，留下一个个小点子。
example.pinyin: Yǔshuǐ dǎ zài chuānghu shàng, liú xià yí gè gè xiǎo diǎnzi.
example.english: Raindrops hit the window, leaving little droplets behind.
example.fact: Contrary to the classic teardrop cartoon, falling raindrops are actually closer to the shape of a hamburger bun — rounded on top and flattened on the bottom — because air resistance pushes up against the drop as it falls. Drops larger than about 4 millimeters across become unstable and break apart into smaller droplets, which is why the biggest raindrops you'll ever see are roughly the size of a housefly.

components.note: 禾 (grain, a rice/wheat plant) — 科 relates to sorting and measuring crops.
斗 (a measuring ladle) — measuring grain into ordered categories gave 科 its meaning 'a branch of study' or 'a department.'
扌 (hand) — relates to 技's meaning 'skill, technique,' a skill performed with the hands.
支 (zhī) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from jì.

example.hanzi: 这家公司专注于人工智能科技的研发。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī zhuānzhù yú réngōng zhìnéng kējì de yánfā.
example.english: This company focuses on researching and developing artificial intelligence technology.
example.fact: The term 'artificial intelligence' was coined in 1956 at a summer workshop at Dartmouth College, where researchers optimistically predicted machines could achieve human-level reasoning within a generation. Progress stalled for decades in periods researchers call 'AI winters,' when funding dried up after early promises went unmet. It took the rise of cheap parallel computing — largely from graphics cards originally built for video games — to make today's large-scale neural networks practical.

components.note: 勹 (an enclosing shape) — wrapping around.
巳 (a baby) — swaddled inside, the image of wrapping something up giving 包 its meaning 'to wrap; bag, package.'
衣 (clothes) — 裹 relates to wrapping something, like fabric around an object.
果 (guǒ) gives the sound — an exact match with 裹.

example.hanzi: 邮递员今天送来了一个很重的包裹。
example.pinyin: Yóudìyuán jīntiān sòng lái le yí gè hěn zhòng de bāoguǒ.
example.english: The postal worker delivered a very heavy parcel today.
example.fact: The Universal Postal Union, founded in 1874, set common rules so a letter or parcel could cross national borders without needing separate postage for each country it passed through. Before that, international mail often required paying multiple, unpredictable fees along the route. Today the UPU coordinates postal service among 192 member countries, one of the oldest international organizations still in operation.

components.note: 工 depicts a carpenter's square or workman's tool — a simple shape that came to represent work and labor.
贝 (shell/money) — 资 relates to wealth, funds, and resources.
次 (cì) gives a hint of the sound — 资 is pronounced zī, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 公司这个月推迟了发工资的时间。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī zhège yuè tuīchí le fā gōngzī de shíjiān.
example.english: The company delayed the payday this month.
example.fact: The word 'salary' comes from the Latin 'salarium,' often linked to an allowance Roman soldiers reportedly received to buy salt, a valuable commodity used for preserving food before refrigeration existed. Whether soldiers were literally paid in salt is debated by historians, but salt was valuable enough in the ancient world to be traded along dedicated routes such as the Via Salaria, the 'salt road' leading to Rome.

components.note: 八 (to divide/split) — represents something being separated into smaller parts.
亅 (a hook/line) — cutting a small piece off, an image tied to the meaning 'small, tiny.'
八 (to divide/split) — represents something being separated into smaller parts.
亅 (a hook/line) — cutting a small piece off, an image tied to the meaning 'small, tiny.'
白 (white, bright) — 的 originally named a bright target or bullseye, a spot marked out for archery practice.
勺 (sháo) echoes 的's older reading dí; the character was later borrowed purely for its sound to write the common grammatical particle de.

example.hanzi: 桌子上放着一个小小的花瓶。
example.pinyin: Zhuōzi shàng fàng zhe yí gè xiǎoxiǎo de huāpíng.
example.english: There's a tiny vase sitting on the table.
example.fact: A nanometer is one billionth of a meter — small enough that roughly ten hydrogen atoms lined up in a row would span the distance. Modern computer chips etch transistor features only a few nanometers wide, meaning billions of them fit onto a chip smaller than a fingernail. At that scale, quantum effects like electron tunneling start to matter, one of the main engineering challenges in shrinking chips further.

components.note: 女 (woman) forms the left side of the character.
彐 depicts a broom — a woman holding a broom, a traditional image of housework, gave 妇 its meaning 'married woman, wife.'
女 depicts a kneeling figure with arms crossed, a traditional posture — a simple picture of a woman.

example.hanzi: 三月八日是国际妇女节。
example.pinyin: Sānyuè bā rì shì Guójì Fùnǚ Jié.
example.english: March 8th is International Women's Day.
example.fact: International Women's Day traces back to 1909, when the Socialist Party of America organized a National Woman's Day in New York to honor a garment workers' strike. The date was fixed at March 8th in 1917 after women textile workers in Petrograd, Russia, staged a strike and protest often credited with helping spark the February Revolution that eventually led to the Tsar's abdication.

components.note: Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'
氵 (water) — 源 originally referred to the spring where a river begins
原 (yuán) gives the sound — an exact match with 源's reading yuán

example.hanzi: 记者一直没有透露这条消息的来源。
example.pinyin: Jìzhě yìzhí méiyǒu tòulù zhè tiáo xiāoxi de láiyuán.
example.english: The reporter never revealed the source of this information.
example.fact: Deep Throat, the anonymous source behind the Watergate scandal reporting by Bob Woodward and Carl Bernstein, kept his identity secret for over 30 years until former FBI associate director Mark Felt revealed himself in 2005. Protecting a source's identity is considered so important in journalism that some reporters have gone to jail rather than reveal one, a principle tested in cases like that of New York Times reporter Judith Miller in 2005.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 判 originally related to cutting something apart to distinguish or decide
半 (bàn) gives a sound close to 判's reading pàn, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
冫 (water) — 决 originally described water breaking through a levee, later extending to the abstract sense of "to decide, resolve."
夬 (guài) is the historical phonetic base for 决's reading jué, a connection faded by centuries of sound change.

example.hanzi: 法官宣读了对被告的判决。
example.pinyin: Fǎguān xuāndú le duì bèigào de pànjué.
example.english: The judge read out the verdict against the defendant.
example.fact: The right to a trial by jury traces back to Magna Carta in 1215, which limited the English king's power to imprison free men without lawful judgment. The number twelve, still standard for many juries today, has no single confirmed origin, though some historians link it to the twelve tribes of Israel or the twelve apostles as symbolically complete groups.

components.note: 足 (foot) — relates to 路's meaning 'road, path,' something walked on with feet.
各 (gè) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from lù.
纟 (thread) — relates directly to 线's meaning 'line, thread, wire.'
戋 (jiān) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from xiàn.

example.hanzi: 我们改变了去机场的路线，避开了堵车。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen gǎibiàn le qù jīchǎng de lùxiàn, bìkāi le dǔchē.
example.english: We changed our route to the airport to avoid the traffic jam.
example.fact: The GPS satellite network relies on atomic clocks accurate enough that a timing error of just one microsecond would translate into a position error of about 300 meters on the ground. Because satellites orbiting at high speed and altitude experience time slightly differently under Einstein's theories of relativity, GPS systems must correct for both special and general relativistic effects, or reported locations would drift by several kilometers per day.

components.note: 土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'
毛 (fur/hair) — 毯 names a woven covering made from fur or wool.
炎 (yán) gives a sound distantly related to tǎn, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 客厅里铺着一块红色的地毯。
example.pinyin: Kètīng lǐ pù zhe yí kuài hóngsè de dìtǎn.
example.english: A red carpet is laid out in the living room.
example.fact: The Pazyryk Carpet, discovered frozen in a Siberian burial mound in 1949, is the oldest known pile carpet in the world, dated to roughly the 5th century BC. Remarkably well preserved by the permafrost, its intricate wool knots — over 3,600 per square inch — show that sophisticated carpet-weaving techniques existed more than two thousand years ago.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 依 relates to a person relying or leaning on something
衣 (yī) gives the sound — 依 is also pronounced yī, an exact match
非 (two things back-to-back) — 靠 relates to leaning against or relying on something
告 (gào) gives a sound distantly related to 靠's reading kào, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 沙漠里的绿洲居民依靠地下水生存。
example.pinyin: Shāmò lǐ de lǜzhōu jūmín yīkào dìxiàshuǐ shēngcún.
example.english: Oasis residents in the desert rely on groundwater to survive.
example.fact: Many desert oases are fed by ancient 'fossil water' aquifers, groundwater deposited thousands to millions of years ago during wetter climate periods and not meaningfully replenished today. Libya's Great Man-Made River project taps such fossil aquifers beneath the Sahara, piping billions of liters of ancient water to coastal cities — a resource that, once drawn down, may take millennia to naturally refill.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — throwing is an action done with the hand.
乃 (nǎi) gives a sound distantly related to rēng, having drifted apart over time.
扌 (hand) — 掉 relates to dropping something from the hand.
卓 (zhuó) reflects an older phonetic connection that has faded in the modern pronunciation diào.

example.hanzi: 他把过期的食物都扔掉了。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ guòqī de shíwù dōu rēngdiào le.
example.english: He threw away all the expired food.
example.fact: Food waste buried in landfills decomposes without enough oxygen, producing methane, a greenhouse gas more than 25 times more potent than carbon dioxide over a 100-year period. The United Nations estimates roughly a third of all food produced worldwide is lost or wasted, which is why some cities now mandate separate composting of food scraps to divert them from landfills.

components.note: 衤 (clothes) — 裸 describes the absence of clothing, being bare.
果 (guǒ) gives a sound close to luǒ, sharing the same rhyme.
亻 (person) — 体 relates to the human body, its physical form.
本 (běn) approximates 体's reading tǐ; this simplified form replaced the traditional 體, which combined 骨 (bone) with a different phonetic element.

example.hanzi: 那座雕像描绘的是一个裸体的战士。
example.pinyin: Nà zuò diāoxiàng miáohuì de shì yí gè luǒtǐ de zhànshì.
example.english: That statue depicts a nude warrior.
example.fact: Ancient Greek sculptors idealized the nude male form in statues like the Discobolus, believing physical perfection reflected moral and civic virtue, a tradition later revived during the Renaissance. Michelangelo's David, carved between 1501 and 1504 from a single block of marble previously abandoned by two other sculptors as flawed, stands over 5 meters tall and remains one of the most famous nude sculptures in history.

components.note: 阝 (a mound, related to terrain) — the ground where something happens.
臽 (a pit) — a hole in the ground, together giving 陷 its meaning 'to sink, to fall into a trap.'
On the left side, 阝 derives from 阜 (mound, earthworks), pointing to something dug into the ground.
井 means 'well' and is pronounced jǐng — the same as 阱 — evoking a deep pit dug into the earth like a well, which gave 阱 its meaning 'pitfall, trap.'

example.hanzi: 猎人在森林里设了一个陷阱。
example.pinyin: Lièrén zài sēnlín lǐ shè le yí gè xiànjǐng.
example.english: The hunter set a trap in the forest.
example.fact: Pitcher plants lure insects with sweet nectar into a slippery, tube-shaped trap lined with downward-pointing hairs that make climbing back out nearly impossible. Once inside, the insect drowns in a pool of digestive fluid at the bottom, which the plant uses to extract nitrogen and other nutrients scarce in the boggy soils where these plants typically grow.

components.note: 八 here depicts something splitting apart or being divided.
厶 is an old form meaning 'private' or 'one's own' — 公 shows dividing up private property to share it fairly, giving rise to the meaning 'public' or 'fair.'
一 (a line, representing a target or standard) — 正 shows a foot arriving exactly at the right mark.
止 (foot, to stop) — arriving and stopping precisely at the target gives 正 its meaning of 'correct' or 'straight.'

example.hanzi: 大家都希望法律能对每个人公正。
example.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu xīwàng fǎlǜ néng duì měi gè rén gōngzhèng.
example.english: Everyone hopes the law can be fair to everyone.
example.fact: The blindfolded figure of Lady Justice, holding a scale and sword, traces back to the Roman goddess Justitia and, further, to the Egyptian goddess Ma'at, said to weigh the hearts of the dead against a feather to judge their worthiness. The blindfold, a later addition dating to around the 16th century, was meant to symbolize impartiality — that justice should not be swayed by who stands before it.

components.note: 口 (mouths) — 总 pictures many voices.
心 (heart, mind) — many mouths brought together under one mind gave 总 its meaning 'overall' or 'to gather together.'
⺮ (bamboo) — the material of ancient counting rods.
具 (held in two hands) — bamboo counting rods or an abacus held up for use, the tools of calculation that gave 算 its meaning 'to calculate, count.'

example.hanzi: 经过三年的努力，他总算通过了考试。
example.pinyin: Jīngguò sān nián de nǔlì, tā zǒngsuàn tōngguò le kǎoshì.
example.english: After three years of effort, he finally passed the exam.
example.fact: Thomas Edison and his team reportedly tested thousands of filament materials before settling on carbonized bamboo for a commercially practical incandescent light bulb in the late 1870s. Edison later described earlier failures not as failures but as having 'found 10,000 ways that won't work,' a mindset historians credit with driving the systematic, trial-and-error approach of his Menlo Park laboratory.

components.note: 直 (straight, upright) — 真 relates to something level and true.
几 (a small table) — an object placed level and true on a table gave 真 its meaning 'real' or 'true.'
心 was originally a pictograph of the physical shape of a human heart, and came to represent the mind, feelings, and intention as well.

example.hanzi: 他真心希望朋友们都能过得幸福。
example.pinyin: Tā zhēnxīn xīwàng péngyǒumen dōu néng guò de xìngfú.
example.english: He sincerely hopes his friends can all live happily.
example.fact: The handshake is believed to have originated as a gesture of peace in ancient times, showing neither party was carrying a hidden weapon in their right hand. Some historians trace depictions of clasped hands, called 'dexiosis,' back to 5th-century BC Greek funerary art, where it symbolized trust and farewell between the living and the dead.

meanings: auxiliary showing sth happened in the past

components.note: Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'

example.hanzi: 你刚才说什么来着？
example.pinyin: Nǐ gāngcái shuō shénme láizhe?
example.english: What did you just say again?
example.fact: The 'tip-of-the-tongue' phenomenon, when you're sure you know a word but can't quite retrieve it, has been studied since psychologists Roger Brown and David McNeill formally named it in a 1966 paper. Brain imaging studies suggest the sought-for word is often stored correctly in memory the whole time — the trouble lies in a temporary failure to link its sound to its meaning during retrieval, not in forgetting the word itself.

components.note: 十 (ten) — suggests something repeated many times.
口 (mouth) — a story passed down through ten generations of mouths gave 古 its meaning 'old, ancient.'
耂 (a person bent with age, with long hair) — depicts an elderly figure.
匕 (here representing a cane or walking stick) — combined with the bent figure above, 老 pictures an old person leaning on a cane.

example.hanzi: 这座古老的城墙已经有两千年的历史了。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò gǔlǎo de chéngqiáng yǐjīng yǒu liǎngqiān nián de lìshǐ le.
example.english: This ancient city wall already has a two-thousand-year history.
example.fact: Contrary to a popular myth, the Great Wall of China is not visible to the naked eye from the Moon — it is only a few meters wide, far too narrow to be seen from such a distance despite its roughly 21,000-kilometer total length across multiple dynasties. Astronauts in low Earth orbit, a few hundred kilometers up, have reported it is difficult to spot even from there without magnification, especially compared to highways or airports.

meanings: (of a turn of events) not too encouraging

components.note: The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
女 (woman) — 妙 originally described a young woman's delicate charm, extended to mean 'wonderful, clever.'
少 (shǎo) gives a sound distantly related to miào, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 天空突然变黑，情况看起来不妙。
example.pinyin: Tiānkōng tūrán biàn hēi, qíngkuàng kàn qǐlái bùmiào.
example.english: The sky suddenly turned black — the situation looked ominous.
example.fact: A greenish tint to the sky before a storm is often associated with hail-producing supercell thunderstorms, caused by sunlight scattering through the storm's massive, deep cloud layers combined with large water droplets and ice. Meteorologists still debate the exact mechanism, but the color has long served as a folk warning sign for approaching severe weather, including tornadoes.

components.note: 亻 (person) shows 伪 describes something false or counterfeit, often about people's actions or claims.
为 (wéi) gives a sound very close to wěi, differing mainly in tone.
衣 (clothing) — 装 relates to clothes, dress, and attire
壮 (zhuàng) gives the sound — 装 is pronounced zhuāng, a close match

example.hanzi: 士兵们用树叶把自己伪装起来。
example.pinyin: Shìbīngmen yòng shùyè bǎ zìjǐ wěizhuāng qǐlái.
example.english: The soldiers camouflaged themselves with leaves.
example.fact: Cuttlefish can change the color and texture of their skin within a fraction of a second using thousands of pigment-filled cells called chromatophores, controlled directly by their nervous system. Remarkably, cuttlefish are colorblind, yet they can still match complex background patterns almost perfectly — a puzzle that has led researchers to suspect they may sense light through photoreceptors in their skin as well as their eyes.

components.note: 宀 (roof) marks the setting — a house or hall.
妟 (a woman 女 beneath the sun 日) suggests ease and comfort — people gathered comfortably under a roof, giving 宴 its meaning 'banquet, feast.'
人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'

example.hanzi: 公司为退休的员工举办了一场宴会。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī wèi tuìxiū de yuángōng jǔbàn le yì chǎng yànhuì.
example.english: The company held a banquet for the retiring employee.
example.fact: Ancient Roman banquets, especially among the elite, could last many hours and feature exotic dishes such as roasted flamingo or stuffed dormice, eaten while reclining on couches rather than sitting at a table. Some wealthy hosts employed a designated slave called a 'nomenclator' whose sole job was to remember and announce the names of arriving guests, a kind of living guest list.

components.note: 禾 (a grain stalk, bending under its own weight) sits above 女.
女 (woman) below suggests a yielding, pliant posture — together evoking something entrusted or handed over, the root of 委's meaning "to entrust, to delegate."
扌 (hand) — a hand held out, palm up
乇 — something resting on the upturned palm for support

example.hanzi: 他委托律师处理这起案件。
example.pinyin: Tā wěituō lǜshī chǔlǐ zhè qǐ ànjiàn.
example.english: He entrusted the lawyer to handle this case.
example.fact: The modern escrow system, where a neutral third party holds funds or documents until conditions of an agreement are met, has roots in medieval English law, where the word 'scroll' (from Old French 'escroue') referred to a written deed held in trust by someone other than the two contracting parties. Real estate transactions worldwide still rely on the same basic idea: a trusted intermediary who releases assets only once agreed conditions are satisfied.

components.note: Originally depicted a burning candle or the sun's rays radiating outward — the source of 白's meaning 'white, bright, clear.'
宀 (roof) — 宫 names a palace, a grand building.
吕 (lǚ) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading gōng has diverged considerably.

example.hanzi: 总统在白宫接见了外国代表团。
example.pinyin: Zǒngtǒng zài Báigōng jiējiàn le wàiguó dàibiǎotuán.
example.english: The president received the foreign delegation at the White House.
example.fact: The White House was originally built with sandstone that was whitewashed to protect it from the elements, one popular explanation for its name, though the name wasn't made official until Theodore Roosevelt did so in 1901. British troops burned the building in 1814 during the War of 1812, and much of the outer stone walls seen today are the same scorched sandstone that survived and was later restored.

meanings: to issue (an official document or credential)

components.note: 发 is a cursive-derived simplification of the traditional 發, whose components pictured an arrow leaving a bow — the sense of something launching or setting out gave rise to meanings like "to send off, to issue, to grow."
关 — a person's arms shown in a waving or embracing gesture, bidding farewell
辶 (to walk) — the person walking away who is being seen off

example.hanzi: 请把这份文件发送到我的邮箱。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhè fèn wénjiàn fāsòng dào wǒ de yóuxiāng.
example.english: Please send this document to my email.
example.fact: The first email was sent in 1971 by computer engineer Ray Tomlinson, who also chose the @ symbol to separate the username from the host computer's name — a convention still used in virtually every email address today. Tomlinson later said he didn't remember the exact content of that first test message and considered the choice of the @ symbol more significant than the message itself.

components.note: 冫 (water/ice) — 冲 relates to liquid, as in pouring or rinsing with water
中 (zhōng) gives a sound close to 冲's reading chōng, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
穴 (a cave/hole) — the den the dog bursts from.
犬 (dog) — a dog suddenly darting out of its den gave 突 its meaning 'sudden, abrupt.'

example.hanzi: 两国因边境问题发生了冲突。
example.pinyin: Liǎng guó yīn biānjìng wèntí fāshēng le chōngtū.
example.english: The two countries had a conflict over the border issue.
example.fact: The Åland Islands dispute between Sweden and Finland in the early 1920s is often cited as one of the first conflicts resolved through the newly formed League of Nations, which granted the islands to Finland while guaranteeing strong autonomy and demilitarization. The arrangement has held peacefully for over a century and is frequently studied as a model for resolving territorial disputes without war.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 指 relates to using the hand, specifically the fingers.
旨 (an aim, purpose) — combined with 扌 (hand), 指 came to mean 'finger' and 'to point,' aiming the hand at something.
A pictograph of an altar or offering table used in ancestor worship — presenting offerings extended to 示's meaning 'to show, display, indicate.'

example.hanzi: 老板给员工下达了新的指示。
example.pinyin: Lǎobǎn gěi yuángōng xiàdá le xīn de zhǐshì.
example.english: The boss issued new instructions to the employees.
example.fact: After a prototype of the Boeing B-17 crashed in 1935 due to pilot error despite the crew's extensive experience, the U.S. Army Air Corps developed the first standardized pilot checklist rather than relying purely on training and memory. That simple written instruction list is credited with helping make the B-17 one of the most reliable aircraft of World War II, and checklists remain a cornerstone of aviation safety today.

meanings: to have no other option but to ...

components.note: 口 (mouth) — the source of speech.
八 here suggests something small or simple leaving the mouth, giving 只 its meaning 'only, merely.'
女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'

example.hanzi: 因为下大雨，我们只好取消了野餐。
example.pinyin: Yīnwèi xià dàyǔ, wǒmen zhǐhǎo qǔxiāo le yěcān.
example.english: Because of the heavy rain, we had no choice but to cancel the picnic.
example.fact: Modern weather radar can detect rain up to about 250 kilometers away by bouncing microwave pulses off water droplets and measuring how the signal returns, a technique developed from radar systems built during World War II. Operators noticed that rain and snow created unwanted 'clutter' on military radar screens meant to detect aircraft, and that same clutter became the basis of the meteorological radar used for forecasts today.

components.note: 散 traditionally depicts a hand (攵) scattering something, like seeds tossed from a basket — the image behind its meaning 'to scatter, disperse.'
止 (a footprint), shown twice — one foot placed in front of the other, the source of 步's meaning 'step, pace.'

example.hanzi: 晚饭后，他喜欢去公园散步。
example.pinyin: Wǎnfàn hòu, tā xǐhuān qù gōngyuán sànbù.
example.english: After dinner, he likes to take a walk in the park.
example.fact: Studies on walking speed and health have found that a brisk pace of roughly 100 steps per minute is associated with measurable cardiovascular benefits, sometimes described informally as a 'cadence-based' threshold for moderate exercise. Other research has linked as few as a couple thousand extra daily steps to a meaningfully lower risk of cardiovascular disease, even without any other change in exercise habits.

components.note: 亻 (an upright person) stands beside its mirror image.
匕 (here an inverted person rather than its usual "spoon" sense) — a person shown right-side-up next to one upside-down pictures transformation, the source of 化's meaning "to change, to become."
女 (woman) — 妆 describes putting on makeup, an action tied to appearance.
丬 gives a sound related to zhuāng, though the connection has drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 她每天早上都要花半小时化妆。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān zǎoshang dōu yào huā bàn xiǎoshí huàzhuāng.
example.english: She spends half an hour putting on makeup every morning.
example.fact: Ancient Egyptians of both sexes commonly wore kohl eyeliner as early as 4000 BC, partly for its believed ability to protect eyes from the sun's glare and ward off infection, in addition to its cosmetic effect. Chemical analysis of ancient Egyptian cosmetic containers has found lead-based compounds that, in small amounts, may have boosted the skin's production of nitric oxide, offering a genuine, if unintended, antibacterial benefit.

meanings: (used to emphasize how good or bad something is)

components.note: 另 (other, separate) — 别 relates to distinguishing one thing from another.
刂 (knife) — cutting things apart to sort them gave 别 its meaning 'to separate' or 'other,' and later, 'don't' as a command.
扌 (hand) — 提 relates to lifting or carrying something by hand.
是 (shì) gives a hint of the sound — 提 is pronounced tí, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.hanzi: 别提这件事了，我现在心情很不好。
example.pinyin: Bié tí zhè jiàn shì le, wǒ xiànzài xīnqíng hěn bù hǎo.
example.english: Don't even mention this — I'm in a bad mood right now.
example.fact: Psychologists have found that suppressing an unwanted thought, sometimes called the 'white bear problem' after a famous 1987 experiment, often backfires and makes the thought return more persistently than if a person had simply let it pass. This 'rebound effect' is one reason therapists frequently encourage acknowledging and naming difficult emotions rather than trying to avoid discussing them entirely.

components.note: A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
午 originally depicted a wooden pestle used for pounding grain; the character was later borrowed for its sound to mark one of the twelve Earthly Branches and, by extension, the height of noon.

example.hanzi: 会议安排在明天上午九点。
example.pinyin: Huìyì ānpái zài míngtiān shàngwǔ jiǔ diǎn.
example.english: The meeting is scheduled for nine oʼclock tomorrow morning.
example.fact: Human body temperature naturally reaches its daily low point in the early morning hours, typically between 4 and 6 a.m., before core temperature and alertness begin climbing as part of the circadian rhythm. This is one reason cognitive performance and reaction times tend to be measurably worse in the pre-dawn hours, a factor implicated in several major industrial accidents that occurred during overnight shifts.

components.note: 刂 (knife) contributes to the character's form, though its link to 剧's meaning 'drama' has faded over time.
居 (jū) gives a rhyme close to jù, with the tone shifted.
阝 (a mound/enclosure) — relates to 院's meaning 'courtyard, institution,' an enclosed place.
完 (wán) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from yuàn.

example.hanzi: 这座剧院能容纳两千名观众。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò jùyuàn néng róngnà liǎngqiān míng guānzhòng.
example.english: This theater can hold two thousand audience members.
example.fact: The ancient Greek Theatre of Epidaurus, built around 300 BC and seating up to 14,000 people, has such precise acoustics that a coin dropped or a match struck on its central stage can reportedly be heard clearly from the very top row. Acoustic researchers have found the limestone seating rows act as a natural acoustic filter, dampening low-frequency crowd noise while allowing higher-frequency sounds like speech to carry clearly.

components.note: 卑 traditionally pictures a hand holding an empty, lowly object — an old image behind its meaning 'low, humble.'
阝 (village) — an older semantic link to a remote, rustic place, hence 鄙's sense of "low, base."
啚 (bǐ) gives the sound — an exact match with 鄙.

example.hanzi: 大家都觉得他的做法非常卑鄙。
example.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu juéde tā de zuòfǎ fēicháng bēibǐ.
example.english: Everyone felt his actions were extremely despicable.
example.fact: The word 'quisling,' meaning a traitor who collaborates with an occupying enemy, comes from Vidkun Quisling, the Norwegian politician who led a puppet government for Nazi Germany during World War II. Quisling was tried and executed for treason in 1945, and his name entered common usage as a byword for betrayal within just a few years of his collaboration becoming public.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — 怀 relates to feelings held close to the heart
不 (bù) gives a sound distantly related to 怀's reading huái, having drifted apart over time
今 (now, the present) — represents what is currently on one's mind.
心 (heart/mind) — keeping the present moment in mind gave 念 its meaning 'to think of, to read aloud, to study.'

example.hanzi: 每次回到老家，他都会怀念童年的时光。
example.pinyin: Měi cì huí dào lǎojiā, tā dōu huì huáiniàn tóngnián de shíguāng.
example.english: Every time he returns to his hometown, he reminisces about his childhood.
example.fact: The 'Proust phenomenon,' named after the novelist Marcel Proust's famous madeleine-and-tea passage, describes how smells can trigger unusually vivid and emotional memories compared to other senses. Neuroscientists have found the olfactory system has a more direct neural pathway to the brain's memory and emotion centers, the hippocampus and amygdala, than sight or sound do, which may explain why a particular scent can suddenly transport someone back decades.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — 宽 originally described a spacious house.
苋 (xiàn) gives a sound distantly related to kuān, having drifted apart over time.
心 (heart) — 恕 describes a heartfelt willingness to forgive.
如 (rú) gives a sound only distantly related to shù today, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 她最终选择了宽恕伤害过她的人。
example.pinyin: Tā zuìzhōng xuǎnzé le kuānshù shānghài guò tā de rén.
example.english: She eventually chose to forgive the person who had hurt her.
example.fact: South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission, established in 1996 after the end of apartheid, offered perpetrators of politically motivated crimes amnesty in exchange for full public testimony about what they had done. Chaired by Archbishop Desmond Tutu, the commission was built on the idea that public acknowledgment of wrongdoing, rather than punishment alone, could help a divided nation move forward.

components.note: 厂 (a cliff or overhang) — 原 relates to a source high up, such as a spring emerging from rock.
泉 (quán) gives a hint of the sound — 原 is pronounced yuán, a connection that has shifted somewhat.
木 (tree) — provides the base image of a tree.
一 (a line) marks the base of the trunk, highlighting the roots — giving 本 its meaning 'root, origin, source.'

example.hanzi: 这条路原本是一条乡间小道。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lù yuánběn shì yì tiáo xiāngjiān xiǎodào.
example.english: This road was originally a small country lane.
example.fact: Rome's Via Appia, begun in 312 BC, was originally built as a military road to move troops and supplies quickly to southern Italy, and sections of its original stone paving are still walkable today, over 2,300 years later. Roman road-building standards required layered foundations of sand, gravel, and fitted stone so durable that some Roman roads remained Europe's best routes for travel well into the 18th century.

meanings: to gain first-hand knowledge of sth

components.note: 冂 (a simplified eye shape in 见's modern form) — emphasizes the act of seeing.
儿 (a person) — a person with an emphasized eye above gives 见 its meaning 'to see.'
讠 (speech) — relates to 识's meaning 'to know, recognize,' knowledge conveyed through words.
只 (zhǐ) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shí.

example.hanzi: 出国留学让他增长了不少见识。
example.pinyin: Chūguó liúxué ràng tā zēngzhǎng le bùshǎo jiànshi.
example.english: Studying abroad broadened his horizons considerably.
example.fact: Astronauts who view Earth from space often report a profound shift in perspective known as the 'overview effect,' first named by author Frank White in 1987 after interviewing dozens of spacefarers. Many describe a heightened sense of the planet's fragility and interconnectedness upon seeing it as a single, borderless sphere hanging in the void, a shift in worldview some report lasting for the rest of their lives.

components.note: 户 (door) — 所 evokes a location or place, such as where a door stands.
斤 (axe) — combined with 户 (door), the image of an axe at a door gave rise to the abstract sense of 'a place' or 'that which.'
亻 (person) plus 乍 (suddenly/for the first time) — together suggesting a person making or doing something for the first time.
户 (door) — 所 evokes a location or place, such as where a door stands.
斤 (axe) — combined with 户 (door), the image of an axe at a door gave rise to the abstract sense of 'a place' or 'that which.'

为 is a simplified, abstracted trace of the traditional 為, which pictured a hand (爪) reaching down to guide an elephant (象) — training the animal to work gave 为 its meaning "to do, to act, to serve as."

example.hanzi: 他必须为自己的所作所为承担责任。
example.pinyin: Tā bìxū wèi zìjǐ de suǒzuòsuǒwéi chéngdān zérèn.
example.english: He must take responsibility for his own conduct.
example.fact: The Nuremberg trials of 1945–1946 established the legal precedent that individuals, including heads of state and military officers, could be held personally accountable for actions committed under orders, rejecting the defense that following superior orders absolves responsibility. This principle, later called the 'Nuremberg principle,' became a foundation of modern international criminal law and influenced the creation of the International Criminal Court decades later.

components.note: 刂 (a knife) — 创 relates to cutting or wounding, extended to mean 'to start, to create,' as a fresh cut marks a new beginning
仓 (cāng) gives a loose sound connection to 创's reading chuàng
心 (heart/mind) — 意 relates to thought, intention, and meaning, things of the mind.
音 (yīn) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading has drifted from yì, though both share a similar vowel.

example.hanzi: 这个广告的创意非常吸引人。
example.pinyin: Zhège guǎnggào de chuàngyì fēicháng xīyǐn rén.
example.english: The creativity of this advertisement is very appealing.
example.fact: The term 'brainstorming' was popularized by advertising executive Alex Osborn in his 1948 book 'Your Creative Power,' which argued groups generate more and better ideas when criticism is deferred until after idea generation. Later research has actually found individuals working alone and then pooling ideas often outperform traditional group brainstorming sessions, partly because people tend to hold back ideas in front of others, a phenomenon researchers call 'production blocking.'

components.note: 亻 (person) — 代 relates to a person's place in time.
弋 (a stake used to mark or catch something) — combined with 亻 (person), 代 came to mean a 'generation' or 'era,' and 'to take the place of' someone.
夫 (man) is shown twice, side by side, one man standing in for another.
日 sits below, together giving 替 its meaning 'to replace, to substitute.'

example.hanzi: 现在很多工厂用机器人代替人工。
example.pinyin: Xiànzài hěn duō gōngchǎng yòng jīqìrén dàitì réngōng.
example.english: Nowadays many factories use robots to replace human labor.
example.fact: The word 'robot' first appeared in Karel Čapek's 1920 play 'R.U.R.,' short for 'Rossum's Universal Robots,' derived from the Czech word 'robota,' meaning forced labor or drudgery. Čapek's robots were biological rather than mechanical, and the play's plot — in which the robots eventually revolt against their human creators — helped establish a theme that has echoed through science fiction ever since.

components.note: A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
士 is thought to depict a broad-bladed battle-axe or ceremonial weapon, a symbol of authority once carried by men of rank — the origin of 士's meaning "a scholar, an officer, a person of standing."

example.hanzi: 现场有不少社会知名人士出席了活动。
example.pinyin: Xiànchǎng yǒu bùshǎo shèhuì zhīmíng rénshì chūxí le huódòng.
example.english: Quite a few well-known public figures attended the event on site.
example.fact: Sociologist Daniel Boorstin coined the term 'celebrity' in its modern sense in his 1961 book 'The Image,' defining a celebrity as 'a person who is known for his well-knownness' rather than for any particular achievement. Boorstin argued mass media had created a new class of public figures whose fame was self-perpetuating, a critique many scholars say became even more relevant with the rise of social media decades later.

components.note: A pictograph of an ancient forked weapon, such as a club or shield-tipped spear — the tool image later extended to 干's meanings 'to do, to work' and, in another reading, 'dry.'
⺼ (flesh) — 脆 originally described flesh that tears or breaks easily.
危 (dangerous) contributes to the character's form, describing something fragile or easily broken.

example.hanzi: 他干脆辞职去创业了。
example.pinyin: Tā gāncuì cízhí qù chuàngyè le.
example.english: He simply quit his job and started his own business.
example.fact: Studies of startup founders have found a surprisingly large share previously worked at just a handful of companies — PayPal's early employees and founders, for instance, went on to start or lead companies including Tesla, SpaceX, LinkedIn, and YouTube, a group often nicknamed the 'PayPal Mafia.' Researchers studying this pattern suggest working closely with other ambitious risk-takers early in a career strongly predicts later founding a company oneself.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — 脆 originally described flesh that tears or breaks easily.
危 (dangerous) contributes to the character's form, describing something fragile or easily broken.
弓 here pictures a young, bent shoot rather than a bow.
冫 (ice/frost) repeated twice suggests two young shoots wilting in the cold, giving 弱 its meaning 'weak, fragile.'

example.hanzi: 玻璃制品非常脆弱，运输时要格外小心。
example.pinyin: Bōli zhìpǐn fēicháng cuìruò, yùnshū shí yào géwài xiǎoxīn.
example.english: Glassware is very fragile, so extra care is needed during transport.
example.fact: Prince Rupert's drops, teardrop-shaped pieces of glass formed by dropping molten glass into cold water, can withstand a hammer blow to the bulbous end thanks to immense internal compressive stress from rapid cooling, yet shatter explosively into powder if the thin tail is so much as scratched. High-speed camera footage has shown the resulting fracture can travel through the glass at speeds exceeding 1,600 meters per second.

components.note: 水 depicts a flowing stream, with a central current and ripples or drops branching off to the sides.
田 (here representing round fruit, not its usual meaning 'field') — 果 pictures fruit hanging from branches.
木 (tree) — fruit growing on a tree gave 果 its meaning 'fruit' and, more broadly, 'result.'

example.hanzi: 市场上卖的水果又新鲜又便宜。
example.pinyin: Shìchǎng shàng mài de shuǐguǒ yòu xīnxiān yòu piányi.
example.english: The fruit sold at the market is both fresh and cheap.
example.fact: Botanically speaking, a banana is classified as a berry, since it develops from a single flower with one ovary and has seeds embedded in its flesh, while a strawberry is technically not a true berry at all — its real fruits are the tiny seed-like specks on the outside. This mismatch between culinary and botanical definitions of 'fruit' and 'berry' trips up even experienced botany students.

meanings: this (referring to a shop, restaurant, or company)

components.note: 辶 (to walk, move) — 这 relates to indicating something nearby, pointing at it as one moves toward it.
文 (wén) is the simplified phonetic element, replacing the traditional 言 found in 這; neither reading closely matches 这's modern pronunciation zhè today.
宀 (roof) — 家 is about a home, the space under a roof.
豕 (shǐ, 'pig') supplies the ancient sound for 家; keeping a pig under one's roof was also a practical sign of a household in ancient China, though the modern readings jiā and shǐ no longer rhyme.

example.hanzi: 这家餐厅的招牌菜是红烧肉。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de zhāopái cài shì hóngshāo ròu.
example.english: This restaurant's signature dish is red-braised pork.
example.fact: Hongshaorou, or red-braised pork, is closely associated with Chairman Mao Zedong, who was said to be especially fond of the dish from his home province of Hunan, and several restaurants there still market versions as 'Mao's braised pork.' The dish's deep reddish color and glossy sheen typically come from caramelizing sugar until it turns a dark amber before the pork is added, a technique distinct from simply darkening the meat with soy sauce.

components.note: 尺 (a ruler/measure) — represents rules or measures being set.
口 (mouth) — measures being discussed aloud in one place gave 局 its meaning 'bureau, office, situation.'
田 (farmland) over 土 (earth/soil) — originally referred to a village or a measured unit of farmland, later extended to mean 'inside' or a unit of distance.

example.hanzi: 局里最近来了一位新局长。
example.pinyin: Jú lǐ zuìjìn lái le yí wèi xīn júzhǎng.
example.english: The bureau recently got a new director.
example.fact: The word 'bureaucracy' comes from the French 'bureau' (desk, office) combined with the Greek suffix '-kratia' (rule, power), coined in the mid-18th century to describe the growing power of desk-bound officials in the French state. Sociologist Max Weber later formalized the concept in the early 20th century, arguing that a bureaucracy's strength — clear hierarchy, written rules, and specialized roles — could just as easily become a weakness when it produced rigid, impersonal decision-making.
